newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says Moody's unlikely to downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says Moody's unlikely to downgrade.

text.p: A Turkish minister said on Friday he did not think Moody's Investors Service would downgrade Turkey's Ba3 sovereign credit rating.

"Moody's is conducting some work on Turkey...But I do not believe Moody's will downgrade. All the indicators show that Turkey's economy is on the way to improvement," Sabri Tekir, the minister responsible for state banks, told reporters.
The Turkish daily Milliyet reported in its Friday edition that Moody's may downgrade Turkey's rating because of a deteriorating fiscal position, high inflation and political uncertainty.
Moody's in London said it had no comment on the newspaper report, which quoted an unnamed senior Moody's official.
The official said Turkey's top economic problem was big budget deficits, adding that the country was in need of tax reform to improve its inefficient taxation system.
Moody's placed Turkey's rating on review for possible downgrade last month because of the poor fiscal situation and the authorities' failure to solve structural problems.

Turkish bankers said the agency may downgrade Turkey's credit rating in late February or early March, following the earlier signals in January. Standard and Poor's cut Turkey's credit rating in December to B from B+. -- Istanbul Newsroom, 90-212-275 0875
